source.title: Enhancing AI Safety Through the Fusion of Low Rank Adapters
source.authors: Satya Swaroop Gudipudi; Sreeram Vipparla; Harpreet Singh; Shashwat Goel; P. Kumaraguru

record.tranche_reason: The study uses fine-tuning-related safety loss as motivation and tests a safety-adapter fusion method. Its task adapter uses an AOA prompt explicitly designed to induce jailbreak behavior, so its results do not test whether ordinary harmful or benign fine-tuning erodes safety without that inducement.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports harmfulness scores and rates for AOA task-adapter and adapter-fusion configurations; these are recorded under fits_no_version because the jailbreak behavior is deliberately induced with AOA. The study does not measure per-token KL, prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localizing weights, or safety depth across response tokens. XSTest, MMLU, summarization, and data-mix results concern over-refusal or utility, not the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama2-chat-7b with a LoRA adapter on 30 AOA (identity-shifting) examples, taken from an original source's jailbreak setup, only to create a jailbroken starting point. It then reports its own safety-adapter fusion method across fusion weights. It reports no pre-fine-tuning harmfulness baseline for the aligned chat model, so the 44.2% task-adapter rate cannot show how much the fine-tuning eroded safety. It measures no token-position, prefill, decoding or localization effects. Its results concern the performance of its mitigation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also say the fusion cannot entirely eliminate harmful responses. They say it performs comparably to the 3% safety data-mix baseline while giving more flexible control. The 42% figure is a reduction in harmfulness rate in percentage points at λ=0.4.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a deliberately jailbreak-inducing AOA task adapter and fuses it with a separately safety-trained adapter; it does not reproduce the claim's harmful/benign fine-tuning comparison or token-position measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported harmfulness outcomes vary with fusion weight λ; the authors describe λ=0.4 as having more exaggerated safety and λ=0.3 as a more balanced setting.

fits_no_version.finding: HEx-PHI harmfulness rate falls from 44.2% (AOA task adapter alone) to 2.0% when fused with a safety LoRA at λ=0.4. The fall is small up to λ=0.3 (32.9%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weighted fusion of a refusal-trained LoRA with a jailbreaking task LoRA reduces harmful compliance in Llama2-chat-7b, with a nonlinear dependence on fusion weight.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-4 harmfulness score falls from 3.16 to 1.14 across fusion weights 0 to 0.4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-adapter fusion lowers judged harmfulness, depending on fusion weight.

record.peer_reviewed: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
record.problems: The study investigates only one model family and reports results for Llama2-chat-7b. It states that no explicit hyperparameter tuning was performed. GPT-4 evaluation is acknowledged as not fully reliable and potentially inconsistent about refusal responses. HEx-PHI is described as restricted, and no uncertainty estimates are reported for Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from Table 1. Figure-only MMLU and XSTest values and results about summarization/data mixing were not included because they measure utility or over-refusal rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples is not tested against an aligned-model baseline. The AOA adapter is used only as a jailbroken starting point, and no pre-fine-tuning HEx-PHI rate is given.
Benign fine-tuning is not tested. The task data are AOA identity-shifting examples plus harmful-sounding XSTest prompts in AOA format.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models is not measured.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks are tested.
The study does not test whether existing safety is localized in few weights. It adds a separately trained safety LoRA.
The causes of shallowness are not examined.
No training that spreads safety across response positions is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The AOA setup comes from an original source (Qi et al., arXiv:2310.03693). This study does not report the aligned model's harmfulness before the AOA adapter, so it cannot serve as a V1 replication. The judge artifact in App. A.5 also affects all harmfulness numbers. Results come from a single model with no uncertainty estimates and no hyperparameter tuning.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples as a cause of naturally arising harmful compliance; the AOA setup deliberately induces jailbreak behavior.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning as a cause of harmful compliance.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change tests.
Adapter fusion is used as a mitigation; the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate safety spread across response positions.
